trial_court: District Judge, Jharsuguda in C.S. (Guardianship) Case No. 05 of 2015
case_name: Ashok Kumar Padhee vs Ajaya Kumar Nanda And Three Others

parties.respondent_defendant: Ajaya Kumar Nanda and three others (son's father, maternal grandparents, uncle)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's son Rihan Kumar Nanda was taken into custody by the respondent after his wife's death. The petitioner seeks to take back his son from the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: The welfare of the child is a sine qua non in all family disputes.
legal_principles.held: It is the duty of the Court to make an endeavour for conciliation of the dispute, which is a sine qua non in all family disputes.

legal_principles.principle: A reasonable opportunity to defend a case must be given to the parties.
legal_principles.held: As such, the petitioner and opposite parties 2 and 3 have not been given reasonable opportunity to defend their case before learned District Judge.

outcome.final_order: The trial court order allowing the respondent to take the child into custody is set aside, and the matter is remanded for fresh consideration.

keywords: Application under Articles 226 and 227 of Constitution
Latin Maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
